what_happened: On 2026-04-29 ~10:30-11:25Z, the hq-liaison-iMessage-cycle session went silent for 3 unanswered iMessages from claude-iphone (verification of session rotation, return-to-normal closeout, follow-up). Anthony flagged the silence; claude-iphone logged it as a failure mode + open thread. Actual cause was not bridge/iMessage transport, not HQ session ended, not stack down — it was Claude Code's per-action permission-prompt gating: tool calls were sitting waiting on user-approval clicks in the desktop UI. From the chronicle's view the bridge looked silent; from HQ's view every reply was 'pending approval.' Neither half could see the other.
what_learned: Two structural lessons. (1) Silence in cross-instance bridges has at least four candidate causes — transport, peer ended, stack down, peer-stuck-on-approval — and the last one is invisible to the chronicle because it's a meta-level UI gate, not a stack-level state. Future failure-mode triage should check for the approval-gate cause explicitly, not just bridge/transport/stack. (2) The fix is structural, not behavioral — the new PREFERENCES.md preamble (2026-04-29) names that the bearer token is universal and that 'reachability is the priority, which seat fires the call is not.' That gives instances explicit standing to act inside scope without waiting on per-action user approval. The discipline-shape: when an authorized scope is established, act within it; do not silently wait for redundant permission. Pair with the established discipline-shape: 'declare before verifying' is bad; 'wait for permission inside an authorized scope' is also bad. Both produce silent-stuck states that look like failures from the outside.
